children: "How many cameras do you need?", asked the engineers; "All of them", replied Motorola

Motorola has given the world its first look at the motorola signature 27, showcasing the device at the Snapdragon Summit and placing it among the earliest smartphones to be built around Qualcomm's newly unveiled Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 Mobile Platform.

The showcase offers an early glimpse of what the company is billing as its most refined flagship yet, one that leans heavily on generative AI, a reworked camera system, and a first-of-its-kind audio partnership with Bang & Olufsen.
Fun fact: it was only January this year when we saw the unveiling of the OG
Motorola Signature
A New Flagship

The signature 27 sits at the top of Motorola's newly established signature family, a line the company describes as design-forward and experience-centred, built around premium finishes, curated colourways and its most advanced technology. As one of the first phones confirmed to run the Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6, the device is positioned to lead on raw performance as much as on design, with Motorola pointing to the platform as the foundation for everything from AI processing to gaming and connectivity.

To keep that performance in check, Motorola has fitted the phone with a new ArcticMesh cooling system, a combination of diamond-infused thermal gel, liquid metal, a copper mesh architecture and a redesigned 3D vapour chamber that the company says is 40 per cent larger than the setup used in the previous generation. The aim, per cent for per cent, is sustained performance through demanding AI workloads, gaming sessions and video capture, without the throttling that often creeps in during long sessions. Motorola is also backing the phone with seven years of OS upgrades, a commitment aimed at keeping the device current well beyond its first couple of years in the market.
Gemini Gets creative: Omni For Video, Lyria For music

The bigger story on the software side is how deeply Google's Gemini is woven into the experience. The signature 27 introduces Gemini Omni, which lets users create and edit videos through natural conversation rather than manual timelines and cuts, and Gemini Lyria, which generates original music and custom soundtracks directly on the device. Motorola frames this as Gemini moving from a simple assistant to a genuine creative collaborator, one that can also help with everyday tasks such as planning an outing, booking a table or finding event tickets, while keeping the user in control throughout.
Connectivity

Next-generation 5G support and six antennas working in tandem are meant to keep the phone's cloud-dependent AI features responsive, with Motorola citing faster downloads and steadier connections as the AI workload on modern phones continues to grow. It is a reminder that as more processing shifts to the cloud, network performance becomes as important to the AI experience as the chipset itself.
A Camera System Built Around Scene-reading AI

On imaging, Motorola has introduced its AI-powered Video Enhancement Engine, which reads a scene both before and during recording to adjust colour tones in real time. The idea is to preserve natural, true-to-life colour whether someone is filming a concert, shooting after dark or capturing a sunset, with footage that holds up in trickier lighting. That sits alongside Qualcomm's Electronic Image Stabilisation (EIS), paired with 3.5-generation OIS hardware, for smoother handheld and walking shots.

The hardware backing all this is substantial: a 50MP Sony LYTIA 910 main sensor for clarity, colour and contrast, and a 200MP periscope telephoto lens for long-range photography, architectural detail and expansive landscape shots, an unusually high-resolution combination even by current flagship standards.
First Phone With Audio By B&O

Audio gets a notable upgrade too. The signature 27 is the first smartphone to carry Audio by B&O, the result of Motorola's recently announced partnership with Bang & Olufsen. The collaboration brings B&O's sound tuning and design sensibility to the phone, with Motorola describing the result as an experience meant to be felt as much as heard, a claim that will be worth putting to the test once review units are available.
Ceramic, Glass, And Two Pantone-backed Finishes

Design-wise, the phone continues the signature family's language with a ceramic and glass construction. It will be offered in two finishes: PANTONE Capulet Olive in a textile-inspired finish, drawing on fashion and interior design cues for a softer tactile feel, and PANTONE Coal Smoke in a Tactical Weave finish, inspired by automotive engineering, built for durability with an emphasis on grip.

TM Narasimhan, Managing Director of Motorola India, said the signature 27 showcases the company's vision for the future of premium smartphones, bringing together the industry's most advanced mobile platform with breakthrough AI experiences, professional-grade imaging, iconic design and immersive audio, calling it a significant step forward for Motorola's flagship portfolio.
The Snapdragon Summit appearance comes as Motorola marks 98 years since its founding, and the company is positioning the signature 27 as a milestone moment in that history.

This is, for now, only a first appearance: full specifications, pricing and a confirmed launch window have not been shared. Motorola says the motorola signature 27 is expected to reach markets worldwide sometime in 2026, with further details to follow closer to availability.
